qs.q: A patient with Klinefelter syndrome (XXY) is noted to have firm subareolar breast enlargement. Which hormonal profile is primarily responsible for the development of gynecomastia in this syndrome?
o: Excessive circulating levels of free testosterone and depleted estrogens
Hypersecretion of luteinizing hormone without any change in sex steroids
Low androgen levels resulting in a relative excess of estrogen
Complete peripheral resistance to all circulating glucocorticoids
qs.e: Klinefelter syndrome is characterized by low androgens and relative estrogen excess, which tips the hormonal balance and causes gynecomastia. Male breast tissue normally remains small because androgens counteract estrogen stimulation.

qs.q: What is the genetic basis and clinical presentation of Klinefelter's syndrome?
o: 5p deletion with high-pitched cat cry and microcephaly
47,XXY karyotype with tall stature and hypogonadism
45,X karyotype with short stature and webbed neck
qs.e: Klinefelter's syndrome results from sex chromosome nondisjunction producing a 47,XXY karyotype in males, marked by tall stature, hypogonadism, and infertility. 45,X describes Turner syndrome.
